subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should the Gateway gain this permanent pre-upgrade security layer and gateway.security configuration surface, and must every newly introduced header or protocol rejection remain opt-in?
rationale: The choice changes the network admission boundary before client and authentication context exists and establishes three long-lived public settings; code review cannot safely select those defaults without owner intent.

options.title: Opt-in raw-header gate
options.body: Add a pre-upgrade helper using original header lines, with every new rejection disabled unless explicitly configured.

options.title: Approve selected defaults
options.body: Make named checks default-on only with explicit compatibility rationale, documentation, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Retain current boundary
options.body: Decline the new settings and keep established origin and authentication enforcement in the connection-admission path.

recommendation.title: Opt-in raw-header gate
recommendation.body: Add a pre-upgrade helper using original header lines, with every new rejection disabled unless explicitly configured.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion identifies this person for the gate-placement and configuration-contract decision, and recent Gateway origin work shows direct involvement.
